rationale: Exclude (E01 - wrong topic). This sociological paper performs a secondary analysis of general public opinion surveys (1989, 2003 and 2012) in Serbia regarding attitudes toward private property and macro-level privatization of state/social property, public services, infrastructure and natural resources, alongside class interests shaping survey research. It does not examine household or community water or sanitation services (C1), any legal/regulatory/utility mechanism governing water or sanitation access (C2), or any water/sanitation service access outcome (C4).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both the narrow rule-type reading and the plain Criterion 2 wording result in exclusion: even if macro-level privatization policy were treated broadly under Criterion 2, the study is a general sociological analysis of public opinion surveys on private property and privatization in Serbia and fails both Criterion 1 (not about household or community water or sanitation services) and Criterion 4 (measures survey attitudes and data comparability rather than water/sanitation access outcomes).

evidence_quotes.quote: declining support to privatization of remaining state and social property, public services, infrastructure and natural resources among majority of respondents in Serbia

The main method of research is secondary analysis of data pertaining to attitudes of representative samples of respondents in Serbia on private property and privatization gathered during surveys conducted in 1989, 2003. and 2012
Research demonstrates that scarcity and insufficient comparability of survey data on attitudes towards private property and privatization
